clips.text: Now that's real gold. Same as these. Look.
clips.script: [thick New York accent, impressed, slow] Now that's real gold. [thick New York accent, proud] Same as these. Look.

clips.text: I'll be back in the winter. I always am.
clips.script: [sly, fading] I'll be back in the winter. [soft, promising] I always am.

clips.text: She'll count them. She counted the folding chairs at Mr. Washington's birthday.
clips.script: [wary, certain] She'll count them. [dry, remembering] She counted the folding chairs at Mr. Washington's birthday.

clips.text: I've seen this movie, you know. The lady who runs the potluck always has something in her basement.
clips.script: [mellow, knowing] i've seen this movie, you know. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, easy, lightly ominous] the lady who runs the potluck always has something in her basement.

clips.text: Tata, I like her.
clips.script: [delighted, sincere] Tata, I like HER.

clips.text: Better. Cut the top deeper next time. It needs somewhere to go.
clips.script: [grudging, instructing] Better. [gruff, coaching] Cut the top deeper next time. [dry, matter-of-fact] It needs somewhere to go.

clips.text: Then she can run the block meeting, because she'd be the first person on this street to keep a promise.
clips.script: [dry, grudging] Then she can run the block meeting, [sharp, deadpan] because she'd be the first person on this street to keep a promise.

clips.text: A ball of mud came through the door and took them. Pan and all.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, brisk, matter of fact] A ball of mud came through the door and took them. Pan and all.

clips.text: But I said PLEASE!
clips.script: [outraged, disbelieving] But I said PLEASE!

clips.text: If this turns out to be a parking meter, I'm going to be upset.
clips.script: [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, gruff, suspicious] If this turns out to be a parking meter, [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, dry, warning] I'm going to be upset.

clips.text: Safest place there is. Gold is for keeping, Cozy Rosie. You put that where nobody's going to look.
clips.script: [thick New York accent, certain, chatty] Safest place there is. [thick New York accent, plain, a rule] Gold is for keeping, Cozy Rosie. [thick New York accent, conspiring] You put that where nobody's going to LOOK.

clips.text: What did you tell her?
clips.script: [curious, eager] What did you tell her?

clips.text: Two padlocks. On a shed.
clips.script: [mellow, quietly thrilled] two padlocks. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, slow, savoring] on a shed.

clips.text: The gold coin is with the biggest thing that woke up. Find it, put it in the hole, and call me when the color comes back.
clips.script: [brisk, instructing] The gold coin is with the biggest thing that woke up. [firm, businesslike] Find it, put it in the hole, [proud, final] and call me when the color comes back.

clips.text: Hm. That one's a loaf.
clips.script: [low, grudging approval] Hm. [gruff, quiet] That one's a LOAF.

clips.text: Who's asking?
clips.script: [sharp, suspicious] Who's asking?

clips.text: Girls, sneakers. Tom, hold the door. Hubby, you stay right there. When we get them back, the first one's yours.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, charge nurse, fast] Girls, sneakers. Tom, hold the door. Hubby, you stay right there. [warm Long Island accent, softer, a promise] When we get them back, the first one's yours.

clips.text: The grass is Boppy color!
clips.script: [delighted discovery] The grass is Boppy color!

clips.text: 'Trim to regulation height.' Bernadette, you taped a notice to my roses.
clips.script: [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, reading, flat] Trim to regulation height. [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, disbelieving, turning] Bernadette, you taped a notice to my ROSES.

clips.text: Good girl. Now. Your grandmother promised me the first muffin. Who's got my muffin?
clips.script: [thick New York accent, pleased] Good girl. [thick New York accent, turning to business] Now. Your grandmother promised me the first muffin. [thick New York accent, looking around] Who's got my muffin?
